name: Question 10
worked_solution:
The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-\frac{f({x}_{n})}{{f}^{′}({x}_{n})}
$$

where ${f}^{′}({x}_{n})$ is the derivative of $f(x)$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=(\operatorname{tan}⁡({x}^{2})-x+1)^{′}=2x{sec}^{2}⁡({x}^{2})-1.
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{n+1} & ={x}_{n}-\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡({x}_{n}^{2})-{x}_{n}+1}{2{x}_{n}{sec}^{2}⁡({x}_{n}^{2})-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=1.8,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡({x}_{0}^{2})-{x}_{0}+1}{2{x}_{0}{sec}^{2}⁡({x}_{0}^{2})-1} \\  & =1.8-\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡({1.8}^{2})-1.8+1}{2(1.8){sec}^{2}⁡({1.8}^{2})-1} \\  & =2.066\,129…\end{aligned}
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡({x}_{1}^{2})-{x}_{1}+1}{2{x}_{1}{sec}^{2}⁡({x}_{1}^{2})-1} \\  & =(2.066\,129…)-\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡((2.066\,129…)^{2})-(2.066\,129…)+1}{2(2.066\,129…){sec}^{2}⁡((2.066\,129…)^{2})-1} \\  & =2.017\,679….\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${x}_{1}≈2.066$ and ${x}_{2}≈2.018,$ rounded to three decimal places.

EXPLANATION

The formula for the Newton-Raphson method is

xn+1=xn−f(xn)f′(xn)

where f′(xn) is the derivative of f(x) evaluated at xn.

In our case, we have

f′(x)=(tan⁡(x2)−x+1)′=2xsec2⁡(x2)−1.

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

xn+1=xn−tan⁡(xn2)−xn+12xnsec2⁡(xn2)−1

Starting with x0=1.8, we have

x1=x0−tan⁡(x02)−x0+12x0sec2⁡(x02)−1=1.8−tan⁡(1.82)−1.8+12(1.8)sec2⁡(1.82)−1=2.066129…

For the second iteration, we have

x2=x1−tan⁡(x12)−x1+12x1sec2⁡(x12)−1=(2.066129…)−tan⁡((2.066129…)2)−(2.066129…)+12(2.066129…)sec2⁡((2.066129…)2)−1=2.017679….

Therefore, x1≈2.066 and x2≈2.018, rounded to three decimal places.
